title: Telling Cultural Stories Through Vietnamese Cuisine
excerpt: Culture and cuisine have always been closely intertwined. Cultural characteristics give dishes their identity and elevate their value, thereby contributing to the sustainable development of the culinary industry.
author: VOV.VN

content.text: When Dishes "Tell Stories"

Vietnam possesses an incredibly rich and diverse culture and cuisine, shaped by its different geographical regions. The cultural differences between the North, Central, and South make Vietnamese cuisine diverse and appealing, with a wide range of flavors, cooking methods, presentation styles, and ways of enjoying food.

The geographical, historical, and long-standing cultural characteristics of each region have influenced the lifestyles and everyday meals of local people. According to MSc. Phan Vu Dieu Binh (Hue Tourism College), culinary culture is reflected in every dish created by people. For example, the folk verse "The chicken clucks with lemon leaves / The pig grunts, asking for onions..." reflects the wisdom of previous generations about combining spices when cooking. In modern cuisine, cultural elements can be seen in the scientific combination of ingredients, culinary philosophies, dietary practices, ways of presenting food, and the culture of enjoying dishes...

MSc. Phan Vu Dieu Binh explains that Hue cuisine has always been closely associated with Hue culture: "Culture makes Hue dishes different from those of other regions, and Hue royal cuisine is also different from the cuisine of other former capitals. Some dishes can only be found in Hue because their ingredients and preparation methods cannot be found in other localities... Hue people are gentle, soft-spoken, and meticulous, and these characteristics are also clearly reflected in the preparation and presentation of their dishes."

content.caption: MSc. Phan Vu Dieu Binh (left) and Hue culinary artisans demonstrating dishes.

content.text: For example, "Bun Bo Hue" can also tell historical and cultural stories to those who enjoy it. Since ancient times, the people of Hue have held many ceremonies and festivals throughout the year, and pork leg dishes were always included in the offerings. After the ceremonies, faced with large quantities of pork legs, people came up with a broth-based dish served with pork legs and rice vermicelli. Over time, the broth was prepared more elaborately and combined with fresh vegetables, creating the Bun Bo Hue we know today.

In Thai Nguyen, the Tay ethnic community in Dinh Hoa also preserves and promotes its distinctive cultural traditions through cuisine. Artisan Le Thi Nga (Thai Hai Ethnic Stilt House Ecological Village Conservation Area) said that in the village, the cultural and culinary traditions of the Tay people are closely connected to everyday life. These traditions are passed down from older generations to younger ones in order to preserve and promote them.

"In the village, traditional culture is always preserved. From a young age, children are taught about our culture, traditional dishes, and the spices used by the Tay people. Through cuisine, we share the cultural traditions and everyday life of the Tay people with domestic and international visitors. Most visitors to the village find Tay dishes well suited to their tastes. In particular, they really enjoy 'Carp Braised with Fermented Glutinous Rice Wine Residue,' a signature dish found only in Thai Hai village. It uses fermented rice wine residue to remove the fishy smell from the carp," said Le Thi Nga.

content.caption: Visitors experiencing the culture and cuisine at the Thai Hai Ethnic Stilt House Ecological Village Conservation Area.

content.text: Promoting the Sustainable Development of Culinary Culture

Both "Bun Bo Hue" and "Carp Braised with Fermented Glutinous Rice Wine Residue" have been nominated by culinary artisans in Thua Thien Hue and Thai Nguyen for the project "100 Outstanding Vietnamese Culinary Dishes," jointly organized by the Vietnam Culinary Culture Association (VCCA) and Masan Consumer. The project aims to collect, restore, preserve, and promote outstanding Vietnamese dishes and beverages.

According to Mr. La Quoc Khanh, Standing Vice Chairman of VCCA, there are still many dishes and unique culinary traditions among local communities that remain unknown to the wider public. Therefore, VCCA is launching culinary research journeys across the country to discover hidden culinary values. Recently, a survey journey to develop outstanding culinary cultural heritage in five northern provinces was held from March 25 to 31 in Nam Dinh, Ha Nam, Thai Nguyen, Phu Tho, and Hanoi.

Following the research phase, the "100 Outstanding Vietnamese Culinary Dishes" project will create a database of dishes associated with culinary artisans, moving toward the development of purely Vietnamese menus that meet international standards. During the voting stage, consumers and a council of culinary artisans will select the most outstanding dishes. Using digital tools, VCCA will create a Vietnamese culinary map connected to tourist destinations, helping elevate Vietnamese cuisine and attract visitors. In this way, tourism and cuisine will go hand in hand and develop sustainably together.

content.caption: A survey journey to develop outstanding culinary cultural heritage in Nam Dinh, Ha Nam, Thai Nguyen, Phu Tho, and Hanoi.

content.text: In addition, experts believe that strengthening the connection among the "four stakeholders"—the government, researchers, farmers, and businesses—will help Vietnamese cuisine reach a wider audience. At Hue Tourism College, MSc. Phan Vu Dieu Binh said that the training programs of the Department of Culinary Management integrate cultural knowledge to help students better understand the cultural values of Vietnamese cuisine: "When teaching students how to prepare dishes, we always incorporate cultural elements. If they only learn cooking in a purely technical way, they will eventually become merely kitchen workers, making it difficult to nurture their passion. In practice, training shows that students are more interested and remember lessons better when they have the opportunity to learn deeply about the cultural and historical stories surrounding the dishes."

title: Top 8 Smoothies for Healthy Skin: Beauty from Within
excerpt: Smoothies that are good for your skin can not only provide hydration and brighten the complexion but also help prevent signs of aging from within. Join Min in discovering a selection of natural smoothies rich in vitamins and minerals to nourish healthy, beautiful skin every day.
author: Vietnam Food Guide

content.text: Fresh and Clean Drinks for Radiant Skin

Smoothies that are good for your skin can not only provide hydration and brighten the complexion but also help prevent signs of aging from within. Join us in discovering a selection of natural smoothies rich in vitamins and minerals to nourish healthy, beautiful skin every day.
I. Healthy, Beautiful Skin Through Natural Nutrition
1/ The Importance of Smoothies and Vitamins for Skin Health

The skin directly reflects your overall health and nutritional habits. When the body lacks vitamins and minerals, the skin can become dry and rough, develop acne, age prematurely, and lose its natural radiance.

Getting essential nutrients from skin-friendly smoothies allows the body to absorb them easily and nourish healthy, beautiful skin according to the "beauty from within" philosophy—achieving lasting beauty from the inside out.
2/ Scientific Evidence and the Role of Lifestyle and Nutrition in Skin Beauty
Many studies have shown that a diet rich in vegetables, fruits, and olive oil can promote healthy skin, improve elasticity, and slow down the aging process.
Vitamins C and E, along with beta-carotene, are important antioxidants that protect the skin from free radicals, UV radiation, and pollution.
Unlike cosmetics, which primarily work on the surface, nutrients from food nourish the skin from within, providing longer-lasting benefits.
II. Min's Top 8 Smoothies for Radiant Skin

Below are 8 carefully selected smoothies based on their levels of vitamins and minerals that benefit the skin. All ingredients are recommended to be sourced from fresh, clean agricultural products meeting VietGAP standards from Min to ensure optimal quality and food safety.
1/ Carrot and Orange Smoothie

Carrots and oranges are rich sources of vitamins A and C and beta-carotene. The beta-carotene in carrots is converted by the body into vitamin A, which has powerful antioxidant properties and supports skin cell regeneration. Vitamin C from oranges stimulates collagen production, helping the skin maintain its firmness and elasticity. This combination not only brightens and evens out the complexion but also provides natural protection against the harmful effects of UV radiation.
2/ Avocado and Banana Smoothie

Avocados are high in vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant and moisturizer, as well as skin-friendly monounsaturated fats. Bananas provide vitamins B6 and C and potassium, helping maintain moisture balance and soften dry, rough skin. This combination acts as a natural "moisturizer" from within, helping restore the skin's protective barrier and effectively reduce irritation.
3/ Strawberry and Yogurt Smoothie

Strawberries are rich in vitamin C and anthocyanins, which can help brighten the skin and provide powerful antioxidant protection. Yogurt contains natural lactic acid, a gentle AHA that helps exfoliate dead skin cells and even out the complexion. The probiotics in yogurt support a balanced microbiome, which may indirectly improve skin health from within and support skin elasticity.
4/ Kiwi and Green Apple Smoothie

Kiwi contains high levels of vitamin C, along with vitamins E and K. Green apples provide quercetin and other powerful antioxidants. This combination supports skin cell regeneration, helps reduce inflammation, strengthens the skin's natural defenses, and supports the body's natural detoxification processes, promoting healthier skin from within.
5/ Tomato, Honey, and Lemon Smoothie

Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that can help protect the skin from UV damage and promote a more even complexion. Combined with vitamin C from lemon and the antibacterial properties of honey, this recipe can be a beneficial choice for oily and acne-prone skin, helping manage excess sebum and reduce the appearance of dark spots and pigmentation.
6/ Pumpkin and Fresh Milk Smoothie

Pumpkin is rich in vitamin A, beta-carotene, and zinc—nutrients that are important for skin regeneration. Protein from fresh milk provides essential amino acids needed for collagen synthesis. This recipe can be particularly beneficial for skin that is delicate, weakened, or lacking vitality.
7/ Pomegranate and Beetroot Smoothie

Pomegranates contain punicalagin and anthocyanins, while beetroot contains betalains—powerful antioxidants that help protect the skin from oxidative stress. This combination may also support healthy blood circulation, helping the skin maintain a naturally rosy and radiant appearance.
8/ Green Vegetable Smoothie

Green vegetables contain vitamin K, folate, and chlorophyll, which may support the body's natural detoxification processes and liver function. This can indirectly support skin health, helping reduce inflammatory acne and enhance the skin's natural radiance.

title: 10 Famous Vietnamese Specialties You Must Try
excerpt: Vietnam never fails to leave visitors longing for more with its countless specialties, each carrying the distinctive flavors and cultural identity of its region. Join Klook as we explore famous Vietnamese dishes that have won over people around the world!
author: Klook

content.text: Vietnamese cuisine is a delicate harmony of flavors and colors, reflecting the country's diverse cultures from north to south. Each region tells its own story through distinctive dishes, from street food to elaborate feasts. Famous for its use of fresh vegetables and aromatic herbs, Vietnamese cuisine is not only nutritious but also wins over international diners with its harmonious combination of ingredients and seasonings.
So, are you ready to discover the most famous specialties from all three regions of Vietnam with Klook?
1. Hanoi Pho

Hanoi Pho is considered a quintessential Vietnamese dish and a source of pride for the country's cuisine. The broth is simmered from beef bones for many hours, creating a naturally sweet and delicate flavor along with the enticing aroma of spices such as star anise, cinnamon, and black cardamom. Soft and silky rice noodles are combined with thinly sliced beef and fresh green onions, creating a harmonious and flavorful dish that is rich without being heavy.
Reference price: VND 40,000 - 70,000 per bowl.
2. Hanoi Bun Cha

Bun cha is one of the dishes that has made Hanoi cuisine famous. The highlight of the dish is minced pork patties and slices of pork grilled over charcoal until golden brown and wonderfully fragrant. The grilled pork is served in a bowl of perfectly balanced sweet-and-sour dipping sauce, accompanied by crisp pickled green papaya. Diners dip fresh rice noodles, grilled pork, and assorted fresh herbs into the sauce, creating an explosion of flavors.
Reference price: VND 45,000 - 75,000 per serving.
3. Hai Phong Crab Red Rice Noodle Soup

A must-try specialty when visiting Hai Phong, crab red rice noodle soup is known for its distinctive red rice noodles, which have a chewy texture and unique aroma. The broth is made from freshwater crabs, giving it a naturally sweet and savory flavor. It is combined with rich crab paste, fragrant betel leaf pork rolls, shrimp, fish cakes, morning glory, and water spinach. Together, these ingredients create a colorful and irresistibly flavorful bowl of crab noodle soup.
Reference price: VND 35,000 - 60,000 per bowl.
4. Ha Long Squid Sausage

Ha Long squid sausage is a specialty and source of pride in Quang Ninh cuisine. It is traditionally handmade using the freshest cuttlefish. Instead of being finely ground in a machine, the squid is pounded by hand to preserve its distinctive chewy and crunchy texture. When fried, each piece turns golden brown and releases an irresistible aroma, with a crispy exterior and a soft, naturally sweet interior full of ocean flavor. This dish is often enjoyed with steamed sticky rice or rice vermicelli.
Reference price: VND 360,000 - 500,000 per kilogram.
5. Lang Son Sour Pho

Lang Son sour pho has a distinctive character that sets it apart from other types of pho. Chewy rice noodles are tossed with char siu pork, crispy-skinned roasted duck, crispy fried sweet potatoes, fragrant roasted peanuts, and, most importantly, a refreshing sweet-and-sour sauce. The sauce is made from vinegar, sugar, garlic, and chili, creating a balanced flavor that stimulates the palate without becoming overwhelming.
Reference price: VND 30,000 - 50,000 per bowl.
6. Lao Cai Thang Co

Thang co is a traditional dish deeply rooted in the cultural identity of the H'Mong people and other ethnic communities in the Northwestern highlands. It is made from the internal organs of horses, or sometimes buffalo or cattle, and simmered for many hours with distinctive mountain spices such as black cardamom, cinnamon, star anise, and doi seeds. Thang co has a rich, savory, fatty, and aromatic flavor and is traditionally enjoyed piping hot.
Reference price: VND 80,000 - 150,000 per pot.
7. Ha Giang Men Men

Men men is a traditional dish closely associated with the daily life of the H'Mong people in Ha Giang, reflecting their resourcefulness and simple way of life. The dish is made from finely ground dried corn, which is then steamed in a traditional wooden steamer. Men men has a distinctive nutty corn flavor, a subtle aroma, and a soft, chewy texture. Local people often eat it as a substitute for rice, accompanied by vegetable soup or other savory dishes for additional flavor.
Reference price: VND 15,000 - 30,000 per serving.
8. Dien Bien Highland Sticky Rice

Dien Bien highland sticky rice is famous for the exceptional fragrance and chewy texture of glutinous rice grown on hillside fields. The grains are plump, glossy, and naturally fragrant with the aroma of freshly harvested rice. To make the dish even more appealing, the sticky rice is often steamed in a variety of vibrant colors using natural leaves, roots, and fruits, creating the famous five-color sticky rice. Besides being visually beautiful, these colors also symbolize good luck and blessings.
Reference price: VND 20,000 - 40,000 per plate.
9. Cao Bang Seven-Spice Roasted Duck

Seven-spice roasted duck is a unique specialty of Cao Bang, captivating diners with its rich and unforgettable flavor. Carefully selected ducks are marinated with seven secret spices before being roasted over hot charcoal until the skin becomes golden and crispy. The meat remains tender, juicy, and naturally sweet, infused with the distinctive flavors of the mountainous region.
Reference price: VND 250,000 - 400,000 per duck.
10. Tan Cuong Thai Nguyen Tea

Known as Vietnam's "finest tea," Tan Cuong tea is a source of pride for Thai Nguyen. The tea leaves are small, curled, and dark green, producing a clear yellow-green infusion when brewed. The tea has a distinctive aroma reminiscent of young sticky rice. Its initially mild astringency quickly gives way to a deep, lingering sweetness that remains on the palate, captivating tea lovers.
Reference price: VND 200,000 - 800,000 per kilogram.

Vietnamese cuisine is the shortest path back "home"—a place where layers of sweet, sour, spicy, and bitter flavors come together in harmony. Vietnamese specialties carry distinctive flavors that serve as a bridge to a deeper understanding of the country's culinary culture and way of life across generations. Even if you have not yet had the chance to explore famous destinations throughout the country, make a stop in Saigon, where you can find a wide variety of delicious dishes from all three regions of Vietnam.

title: The Meaning of the Vietnamese Family Meal
excerpt: As we know, the family is the foundation of society, where each person is nurtured, shaped, and educated. Strong families create a strong society. The family is a source of support for everyone because it is where unconditional love and protection from parents can be found. Vietnamese families are closely associated with family meals and simple home-cooked dishes filled with the comforting flavors of home, such as water spinach soup and young green papaya or eggplant pickled in soybean sauce.
author: Soc Trang Newspaper

content.text:
The family is where we grow up, surrounded by the mother's sweet lullabies:
"Sleep peacefully, little one,
While Mother goes to work in the distant fields."
Everyone's life is always filled with worries and responsibilities, but whenever we think of family, we cannot help but feel emotional and nostalgic. Perhaps the most cherished memory for everyone is a family meal with all members gathered around the table. Whether the meal is simple or filled with delicious dishes, no one can forget the image of a hardworking mother carefully preparing food for every member of the family, alongside a father drenched in salty sweat as he works hard to earn enough money to provide nutritious meals for his children. There is also the familiar image of brothers and sisters playfully competing for the last pieces of fish or meat on the plate, accompanied by carefree, joyful laughter. All these memories represent the boundless love that family members share with one another. The family meal is the culmination of the family's hard work and a place where knowledge, values, morals, and ways of life are passed down. Older generations share their life experiences and teach younger generations what is right and good, while family members demonstrate filial respect and gratitude toward their grandparents and parents. It is also a place where emotional bonds between family members grow stronger, allowing everyone to work together toward building a progressive and happy family.

What could be happier than living in the love of those closest to us, breathing in the aroma of dishes prepared by our mother, and sitting around the family table while listening to our father's advice: "You must study hard, my child." Happiness is beyond measure when a mother cares for her children and prepares the dishes her family loves, and when a father watches his children grow up, succeed, and find happiness. That is why the family meal is a place where the traditional cultural values of Vietnam, as well as those of each individual family, are kept alive.

content.caption: An illustration of a family meal

content.text: The family meal is also a key to happiness because it brings family members closer together, washes away the day's fatigue, and helps everyone put aside anger and misunderstandings. Around the table, each person can feel protected and cared for, freely express their wishes, and receive thoughtful guidance. The family preserves some of life's most beautiful moments, where everyone gets the chance to be the main character in their own story. Loving one's family means appreciating the advice passed down by grandparents, feeling more deeply the love of parents reflected in clothes faded by years of rain and sunshine, and longing to return home—to be comforted and cared for just as we were during childhood around the family meal.

The meaning of the "Warm and Loving Family Meal," commemorated on Vietnamese Family Day (June 28), once again highlights the extremely important role and meaning of the family, especially the family meal. Therefore, we should cherish every warm and happy moment with our loved ones and maintain the tradition of family meals, because they are where love shines, grows, and spreads.
Source: "Electronic Information Portal of the Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism of Soc Trang Province"

title: Traditional Dishes That Are Essential During Tet
excerpt: TPO - During Lunar New Year, each region of Vietnam has its own distinctive traditional feast. While the North traditionally features pickled onions, Vietnamese pork sausage, and fried spring rolls, Central Vietnam is known for pickled vegetables, sour shrimp, and beef sausage. Traditional Tet feasts are not only diverse in their dishes but also place great emphasis on presentation and color. Let's explore these traditional dishes through the article below:
author: Do Quyen

content.text: 1. Banh Chung

An old Vietnamese saying goes: "Fatty pork and pickled onions, red calligraphy; New Year poles, firecrackers, and green banh chung." Banh chung is considered the soul of Tet and is one of the oldest traditional cakes in Vietnamese culinary culture. It is made from high-quality glutinous rice, pork, and mung beans, wrapped into a square shape in dong leaves and boiled for approximately 8–10 hours until fully cooked. The cake is soft and fragrant with the aroma of glutinous rice and has a distinctive green color from the dong leaves.
2. Pickled Onions

Along with fatty pork and banh chung, pickled onions are an indispensable dish during traditional Vietnamese Tet. They are usually pickled only once a year for Tet. Served alongside other dishes, pickled onions help prevent the meal from feeling too rich, especially when paired with oily and fatty foods.
3. Vietnamese Pork Sausage

Gio lua, also known as Vietnamese pork sausage or cha lua, is made from two basic ingredients: finely pounded lean pork and high-quality fish sauce. The mixture is wrapped in banana leaves and boiled until cooked. Gio lua is considered both a common and elegant Vietnamese dish. It is also enjoyed throughout the year, not just during Tet. When served at a feast, the sausage is usually sliced into neat circular pieces, making it attractive and easy to pick up.
4. Fried Pork Head Sausage

Gio xao is a traditional Vietnamese dish made primarily from pork head meat, which is stir-fried with ingredients such as wood ear mushrooms, black pepper, and salt before being wrapped and tightly pressed into shape. Originating in northern Vietnam, it has now become popular throughout the country.
5. Gac Sticky Rice

According to traditional Vietnamese beliefs, red is the color of good fortune and romantic happiness. Therefore, during full-moon days, special occasions, and especially Tet, a plate of gac sticky rice is considered essential. Gac sticky rice is made from high-quality glutinous rice mixed with fresh gac fruit and steamed until cooked. The finished rice has a beautiful, vibrant red color that is both attractive and symbolic of good luck.
6. Boiled Chicken

Boiled chicken is an indispensable dish on the Tet feast table. Traditionally, Vietnamese people believe that chicken brings good luck and a favorable beginning to the new year. Fresh, high-quality chickens are selected, cleaned, and boiled with spices such as Sichuan pepper, star anise, and ginger. Properly boiled chicken has golden skin without tearing and is served with a dipping sauce made from salt, lime, and chili. The tender, fragrant chicken combined with lime leaves and the salty, sour, and spicy dipping sauce creates an unforgettable flavor.
7. Fried Spring Rolls

Fried spring rolls are considered a simple yet elaborate Vietnamese dish because they require many ingredients, although there is no fixed recipe. The outside is golden and crispy, while the filling contains meat, wood ear mushrooms, vegetables, and bean sprouts. The dish is loved by many people and is often regarded as a quintessential part of Vietnamese cuisine. Today, there are many variations, such as seafood and vegetarian spring rolls, but traditional fried spring rolls remain the most popular.
8. Dried Bamboo Shoot Soup

A bowl of bamboo shoot soup is an essential part of the Tet feast. There are many types of bamboo shoots, such as shredded bamboo shoots and leafy bamboo shoots, but the most common choice for Tet meals is dried bamboo shoots cut into pieces resembling a pig's tongue. Bamboo shoot soup cooked with pork trotters is an indispensable dish for people in northern Vietnam and Hanoi during Tet. It also reflects an ancient Vietnamese culinary tradition of enjoying ingredients derived from nature, such as bamboo shoots and tubers. Without this dish, the meal would lose much of its distinctive Tet character.
9. Vietnamese Frozen Pork and Meat Jelly

Thit dong is a traditional dish commonly enjoyed by people in northern Vietnam during the beginning of the year. Local families often use pork trotters, pig ears, chicken, or duck to prepare it. Thit dong is a dish uniquely associated with spring in northern Vietnam and tastes even better in cold weather. It is typically made from pork, sometimes combined with chicken and pork skin, and all the ingredients are simmered until tender. After being left to cool overnight, the dish naturally sets into a delicious meat jelly.
10. Fermented Pork Sausage

For generations, people in Thanh Hoa have considered fermented pork sausage a meaningful and convenient gift to give to relatives and friends during Tet, expressing sincere affection. Some explain that the dish was traditionally offered to ancestors and associated with wishes for good fortune and prosperity because it was once prepared as a royal offering during Tet. If you visit Central Vietnam during Tet, locals may invite you to enjoy a few small glasses of rice wine accompanied by grilled fermented pork sausages. This specialty is made from pork seasoned with spices, wrapped in guava leaves or leaves of the Indian jujube tree, and left to ferment for several days until it develops a mildly sour, crunchy, and slightly spicy flavor.
11. Banh Tet

Banh tet symbolizes the harmony and union of heaven and earth and is one of the essential traditional dishes on the Tet feast table in Central Vietnam. While northern Vietnam has banh chung wrapped in dong leaves, banh tet in Central and Southern Vietnam is wrapped in banana leaves. Although the ingredients are similar, banh tet is rolled into a cylindrical shape. It is usually sliced into rounds and can be easier to serve after cooking because the cylindrical shape makes it easier to roll and press.
12. Pickled Vegetables

While northern Vietnam has pickled onions during Tet, Central Vietnam has its own version known as dua mon. Made from a combination of ingredients such as daikon, carrots, cucumber, green papaya, and scallions, it creates an irresistible dish full of flavor. Although it may sound simple, making colorful and flavorful pickled vegetables requires considerable time and attention to detail. Soft and chewy slices of banh tet paired with crunchy, slightly sour pickled vegetables create a refreshing and unforgettable taste that is uniquely associated with Tet.
13. Sour Shrimp

Another indispensable dish on the Tet feast table in Central Vietnam is sour shrimp, a specialty of Hue. The dish combines the natural sweetness and nuttiness of shrimp, the richness of pork, the spicy and aromatic flavors of galangal, garlic, and chili, the sourness of star fruit, the slight bitterness of fig, and the fragrance of fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a captivating "symphony of flavors" that leaves a lasting impression on anyone who tries it.
14. Vietnamese Beef Sausage

At traditional New Year gatherings in Central Vietnam, a slice of pinkish-red beef sausage is often served to guests. Its combination of salty, sweet, chewy, and spicy flavors, together with the strong aroma of black pepper, makes it an indispensable dish during Tet and other festive occasions.
15. Fish Sauce-Marinated Pork

During Tet, fish sauce-marinated meat is one of the most popular traditional ways of preserving meat in many provinces of Central Vietnam. Either pork or beef can be used. After preparation, the meat is soaked in a mixture of fish sauce and sugar cooked according to a specific ratio. The meat has a salty and sweet flavor and is usually served with pickled vegetables, pickled scallions, fresh vegetables, and aromatic herbs.
16. Pickled Scallions with Dried Shrimp

While pickled onions are an essential part of the traditional Tet meal in northern Vietnam, people in the South cannot imagine Tet without a jar of pickled scallions or a plate of dried shrimp mixed with sweet-and-sour pickled scallions. Unlike in Central Vietnam, pickled scallions in the South are not usually eaten with banh tet but are instead served with dried shrimp as a separate dish.
17. Coconut Braised Pork with Eggs

Among the many delicious dishes found in Saigon, one of the most famous traditional Tet dishes is coconut braised pork with eggs, also known as pork braised in coconut water with eggs. In the days leading up to Tet, alongside preparing banh tet, families often prepare a large pot of this dish. The combination of tender pork and eggs looks appetizing, is easy to enjoy, and is especially flavorful. To balance its richness, it is commonly served with pickled bean sprouts.
18. Vietnamese Sausage

One of the most popular foods in Southern Vietnam is Vietnamese sausage, known locally as lap xuong. Every Tet, demand for this sausage rises, and it is a familiar part of the Southern Vietnamese family meal. There are many varieties, including fresh, dried, lean pork, shrimp, and fish sausages. Originally from China, lap xuong has become widely loved in Vietnam. It is made from finely ground lean pork and pork fat mixed with rice wine and sugar, then stuffed into dried pork intestines and naturally fermented. This fermentation process gives the sausage its characteristic slightly sweet flavor.
19. Bitter Melon Soup Stuffed with Pork

For Southern Vietnamese families, bitter melon soup stuffed with pork is a familiar everyday dish. It is also prepared during Tet, where it carries the symbolic meaning of leaving hardships behind. In addition, it is considered a nutritious and refreshing dish that can help cool the body during the festive season.
20. Pickled Bean Sprouts

With its refreshing quality and crisp texture, pickled bean sprouts are a popular choice for cooling down during the Tet holiday. They can be eaten with rice or wrapped in rice paper, but they pair especially well with braised pork and eggs because they effectively balance the richness of the dish. The main ingredients are bean sprouts, chives, and carrots, making this a nutritious addition to the Tet meal.

title: Vietnam Ranks Among the Top 3 Healthiest Cuisines in the World
excerpt: Recently, CNN ranked the world's healthiest cuisines, with Vietnam coming in third after Greece and the U.S. state of California. Let's explore what makes these cuisines some of the healthiest in the world!
author: Golden Spoon

content.text: 5. India

Indian cuisine is incredibly diverse in terms of ingredients, flavors, and cooking methods. It is also well known for its distinctive combination of spices. Besides creating an enticing flavor for dishes, many spices also have anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties.

In particular, Indians tend to avoid frozen foods because the natural structure of food can change significantly during the freezing process. They prefer cooking with fresh ingredients, which they believe can help prevent certain diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and other degenerative conditions.
In addition, deep-fried foods and rich ingredients such as butter and cream are relatively uncommon in Indian cuisine.
4. Japan

Japanese people consistently rank among the world's longest-living populations, with an average life expectancy of between 79 and 86 years. In addition, Japan has one of the lowest rates of obesity, with only about 3% of its population classified as obese, compared with 32% in the United States.

So, what is the secret behind Japan's longevity? A balanced approach to eating, combining appropriate calorie intake with satisfying meals, along with nutrient-rich diets, is considered one of the keys to good health. Japanese people eat plenty of vegetables, fish, and foods kept as fresh as possible. They also consume brown rice instead of white rice and rarely use oil or butter, which are high in calories, in their meals.
3. Vietnam
With a cuisine shaped by cultural influences from around the world, along with the habit of using plenty of vegetables and seafood in cooking, Vietnam proudly ranks first in Asia for healthy cuisine.

Most Asian cuisines make extensive use of spices and herbs, and Vietnam is no exception. However, the benefits they bring to each meal are particularly remarkable. In Vietnamese dishes, spices are not merely used to enhance the flavor; they are also an essential part of the dish.

Through delicate combinations, common herbs and aromatic greens create an explosion of flavors in Vietnamese dishes. In addition, Vietnamese cuisine is characterized by light, naturally sweet flavors and relatively little oil, while still being incredibly flavorful and delicious.

content.caption: Fresh spring rolls with shrimp and pork

content.text: 2. California

The only non-country on the list, the most populous U.S. state nevertheless takes second place thanks to its distinctive healthy cuisine. With its diverse geography and multicultural, multiethnic population, California has adopted and combined culinary traditions from many parts of the world, with Mediterranean cuisine playing a central role.

Fresh and flavorful salads combined with heart-healthy olive oil, along with homemade dressings and sauces, form an excellent foundation for the local cuisine. Like many other healthy cuisines, California's food also limits calories and fat by reducing the amount of salt and cheese used in meals.
1. Greece

Greek cuisine is a Mediterranean cuisine that is also diverse and rich due to influences from various culinary traditions, including southern France, Italy, and the Middle East. Olive oil is a defining ingredient and is present in most Greek dishes.

From stews to soups, and from the most elaborate dishes to the simplest ones, traditional Greek cuisine combines the freshest and most distinctive ingredients from the land and sea to create nutritious and high-quality meals. It is built around foods that are rich in color and flavor, packed with nutrients, and relatively low in animal fat.

title: Top 11 Vietnamese Dishes Foreign Travelers Will Never Forget
excerpt: Top 11 Vietnamese dishes that foreign travelers will never forget
author: Sao Star

content.text: 1. Mi Quang
Made with simple, easy-to-find ingredients such as noodles, peanuts, pork, and a distinctive broth, Mi Quang was born and has become a culinary pride of Quang Nam Province.
This dish is served everywhere, from casual street-side stalls to upscale restaurants, winning the hearts of many diners.
2. Pho

Pho is considered one of the quintessential dishes of Vietnam. Millions of bowls of pho are served every day across the country, making it a favorite among both Vietnamese people and international visitors.
In September 2007, this iconic Vietnamese dish was officially added to the Oxford English Dictionary in its familiar form, “Pho.”
3. Fresh Spring Rolls

Fresh spring rolls are a perfect choice for a light meal in Vietnam, with key ingredients including shrimp, rice vermicelli, pork, and fresh vegetables. Some visitors may initially find them slightly challenging to eat because they are not accustomed to the chewy rice paper wrapping.

However, when paired with a delicious peanut dipping sauce, the rice paper becomes softer and easier to bite into, making the overall flavor much more enjoyable. With prices starting at only VND 5,000–10,000 per roll, this dish is affordable and accessible to everyone.
4. Beef in Red Wine Sauce

This is a favorite dish for breakfast or lunch among many Vietnamese people. Beef is slowly simmered and seasoned with fish sauce, sugar, and coconut water, then cooked with onions, carrots, and fresh herbs to create an unforgettable flavor.
A popular way to enjoy this dish is to tear pieces of baguette and dip them into its rich and flavorful sauce.
5. Bun Cha

Bun cha is a famous specialty from Hanoi. Its main ingredients are rice vermicelli, grilled pork patties, seasoned fish sauce, and fresh herbs. Despite its simple and uncomplicated preparation, the dish is exceptionally delicious and has become a favorite among many foreign visitors.
6. Fried Spring Rolls

Made with rice paper wrappers filled with minced pork, vegetables, and eggs, these rolls are fried until golden and crispy. Fried spring rolls, also known as cha gio, are extremely popular in Vietnam and can be found in many restaurants around the world.
7. Broken Rice

Made from broken rice grains, Com Tam is a must-try dish for visitors to Ho Chi Minh City. It is a popular choice for millions of people because it provides a satisfying combination of meat, rice, and vegetables.
8. Bun Bo Hue

Among the many delicious dishes in Hue, Bun Bo Hue has become a favorite among diners. A bowl of this noodle soup brings together all four basic flavors: sour, spicy, salty, and sweet. The broth is simmered with beef bones and lemongrass, then seasoned with fish sauce according to a traditional recipe. Plenty of chili is added to create its characteristic spiciness, as people in Hue are well known for their love of spicy food.
9. Banh Mi

This iconic street food has appeared prominently on the world's culinary map, making it something no visitor to Vietnam should miss. Millions of banh mi sandwiches are baked and sold every day, with many Vietnamese people enjoying them primarily for breakfast. Affordable and delicious, banh mi is a wonderful way to start the day.
10. Caramelized Fish in a Clay Pot

Golden-brown pieces of fish slowly braised in a simple clay pot make for a truly delightful dish. After being carefully marinated and simmered over low heat, the fish is served with steamed white rice. This dish can be found in many restaurants and often impresses visitors with its tender texture, rich aroma, and naturally sweet flavor.
11. Banh Xeo

Many visitors mistakenly think that the crispy outer layer of banh xeo is made with eggs. In fact, it is made from rice flour and turmeric. Filled with shrimp and pork, wrapped in lettuce and fresh vegetables, then dipped into sweet and sour fish sauce, every bite delivers an explosion of delicious flavors.

title: Saigon Food Tour: What to Eat and Where to Go? A Detailed Itinerary
excerpt: A Saigon food tour with a variety of delicious dishes not only satisfies your taste buds but also offers fascinating experiences of local cuisine. If you are planning a food tour in Saigon, save this list of must-try dishes and dining spots that you should not miss.
author: Vin Wonders

content.text: 1. What to Eat on a Saigon Food Tour? 10 Must-Try Dishes
1.1. Broken Rice (Cơm Tấm)

A Saigon food tour would not be complete without the humble yet delicious broken rice. Saigon broken rice (cơm tấm) is a traditional dish that has been closely associated with the childhood memories of many city residents. A delicious plate of broken rice typically comes with small rice grains, cucumber, pickles, a fragrant grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, and steamed egg meatloaf. It is served with a sweet and slightly thickened fish sauce.
Recommended places:

items: Ba Ghien Broken Rice: 84 Dang Van Ngu, Ho Chi Minh City
Ba Ha Broken Rice: 389 Hung Phu, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.2. Bánh Mì

Saigon bánh mì is one of the most popular and affordable street foods, familiar to both locals and visitors. In Saigon, you can easily find bánh mì carts and shops of all sizes on almost every street. The bread has a crispy crust, while the filling comes in many varieties, including grilled pork, roasted pork, beef sausage, Vietnamese pork sausage, fish cake, pâté, butter, cucumber, and pickled vegetables…
Recommended places:

items: Huynh Hoa Bánh Mì: 26 – 30 – 32 Le Thi Rieng, Ho Chi Minh City
Bui Thi Xuan Bánh Mì: 122E Bui Thi Xuan Street, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.3. Hủ Tiếu (Vietnamese Rice Noodle Soup)

Saigon hủ tiếu, also known as hủ tiếu gõ, is a familiar and beloved dish among students, workers, tourists, and residents of Ho Chi Minh City. This simple dish is closely associated with the memories of many people whenever they think of Saigon. A typical bowl of hủ tiếu includes rice noodles and a broth simmered from bones and white radish, topped with lean pork, beef balls, bean sprouts, and chives. It is definitely one of the must-try dishes on a Saigon food tour.
Recommended places:

items: My Tho Thanh Xuan Hủ Tiếu: 62 Ton That Thiep, Ho Chi Minh City
Thanh Dat Nam Vang Hủ Tiếu: 34 Co Bac, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.4. Snails

The Saigon food tour continues with visits to affordable Saigon snail restaurants. In Saigon, you will come across many roadside snail restaurants with dishes starting at around VND 30,000. These places offer a wide variety of fresh snails and shellfish prepared in different ways, such as garlic-fried sweet snails, steamed mud creeper snails, green pepper grilled snails, scallops, grilled oysters with scallion oil, garlic-fried snails, and salt-and-chili crab claws. Saigon's snail restaurants are also popular gathering spots where people can get together and enjoy casual food and drinks after work.
Recommended places:

items: Oc Nhu: 650/4/29 Dien Bien Phu, Ho Chi Minh City
Oc Hoa Truong Sa: 1432 – 1446 – 1460 Truong Sa, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.5. Bún Bò Huế

Bún bò Huế came to Saigon with people from Hue who moved there to build their lives and eventually became a familiar breakfast, lunch, and dinner dish among Saigon residents. During a Saigon food tour, many people choose to try bún bò Huế. Some restaurants in Saigon preserve the original Hue flavor, while others make small adjustments to suit the local Southern palate. The dish appeals to diners with its rich and mildly spicy broth, pleasantly chewy rice noodles, and generous toppings of beef, pork knuckles, Vietnamese pork sausage, and fresh vegetables.
Recommended places for delicious bún bò Huế in Saigon:

items: Co Nhu Bún Bò Huế: 274/29 Vo Van Tan, Ho Chi Minh City
Hanh Bún Bò Huế: 135 Banh Van Tran, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.6. Vietnamese Savory Crepes (Bánh Xèo)

Saigon is a place where the culinary traditions of many regions come together. Bánh xèo is one of the dishes that should not be missing from any Saigon food tour. Saigon bánh xèo mainly comes in two styles: Central Vietnamese bánh xèo and Mekong Delta bánh xèo. Mekong Delta bánh xèo is large, rich, and generously filled with shrimp, pork belly, mushrooms, mung beans, and bean sprouts. Central Vietnamese bánh xèo is smaller, roughly the size of an adult's hand, and is usually filled with bean sprouts and pork or seafood such as squid and shrimp. Bánh xèo is served with plenty of fresh herbs and a flavorful sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
Recommended places:

items: Ngoc Son Bánh Xèo: 103 Ngo Quyen, Ho Chi Minh City
Bánh Xèo 46A: 46A Dinh Cong Trang, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.7. Rice Paper Salad (Bánh Tráng Trộn)

Saigon bánh tráng trộn is made from simple ingredients such as shredded rice paper, quail eggs, shredded green mango, dried beef, Vietnamese coriander, dried shrimp, shredded papaya, and peanuts. Tamarind sauce or calamansi juice is added before everything is mixed together. This familiar street snack costs as little as VND 10,000 and is widely sold along streets, in food areas, near schools, and at traditional markets.
Recommended places:

items: Chu Vien Bánh Tráng Trộn: 38 Nguyen Thuong Hien, Ho Chi Minh City
Co Nam Bánh Tráng Trộn: 45 Le Thi Hong, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.8. Beef Offal Stew (Phá Lấu Bò)

Saigon beef phá lấu is made mainly from beef offal such as tendons, spleen, intestines, honeycomb tripe, and omasum. It is cooked with ingredients and spices including coconut milk, five-spice powder, basil leaves, curry powder, garlic, satay, and ginger. It is usually served with bánh mì or noodles. With its distinctive flavor, this dish makes a Saigon food tour even more enjoyable and memorable.
Recommended places:

items: Co Thao Beef Phá Lấu: 243/29G Ton Dan, Ho Chi Minh City
Beef Phá Lấu: 533 Ba Hat, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.9. Phở (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)

Another must-try dish on a Saigon food tour is phở. Phở is traditionally associated with Hanoi cuisine. After making its way to Saigon, the dish gradually became a familiar favorite among locals and visitors. Saigon phở is often divided into Southern-style and Northern-style phở. Northern-style phở restaurants tend to emphasize the natural flavors of the ingredients, while Southern-style phở has a sweeter and richer broth and is served with plenty of bean sprouts, fresh herbs, and sliced onions.
Recommended places:

items: Pho Hoa Pasteur: 260C Pasteur, Ho Chi Minh City
Pho Le: 415 Nguyen Trai, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 1.10. Crab Soup (Súp Cua)

Crab soup is an incredibly popular light dish in Saigon. The soup is typically made with a broth simmered from bones, corn, snow fungus, crab meat, chicken, and other ingredients. It is cooked until thick and creamy, then topped with quail eggs, cilantro, and pepper. To make the dish even more nutritious, some places also add pork brain, imitation crab, century eggs, and other ingredients. The soup has a rich, savory flavor that keeps your taste buds wanting more. Don't miss crab soup on your Saigon food tour!
Recommended places:

items: Ut Tuyen Crab Soup: 162 Nguyen Thi Nho, Ho Chi Minh City
Trang Crab Soup: 210 Van Kiep Street, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: 2. Must-Visit Food Tour Destinations in Ho Chi Minh City
2.1. Ben Thanh Market

Ben Thanh Market is one of the most appealing destinations for a Saigon food tour. It is considered a culinary paradise in Saigon, bringing together countless delicious dishes from different regions across Vietnam. Here, you can try bánh mì, bánh cuốn, various sweet soups, bún bò Huế, phở, bánh tráng trộn, phá lấu, crab soup, and many other dishes. The market has a wide variety of food stalls at affordable prices, allowing visitors to enjoy as much as they like.
2.2. Chinatown Food Street in District 5

District 5 – Cho Lon is a place where the culinary heritage of Saigon comes together, with many traditional dishes that have been enjoyed for generations. A Saigon food tour here takes you through dishes that blend Vietnamese flavors with Chinese culinary traditions. The Chinatown food street in District 5 offers a wide range of dishes, including shumai, har gow, chicken sticky rice, hủ tiếu, wonton noodles, herbal duck noodles, Chinese chive cakes, crab soup, stuffed bitter melon and chili, herbal black chicken soup, and various traditional Chinese sweet soups. The area is home to countless food stalls and street vendors, ranging from affordable eateries to upscale restaurants serving premium and nutritious specialties.
2.3. Ho Thi Ky Food Street

Ho Thi Ky Food Street is one of the most famous destinations for Saigon street food. Along this approximately 100-meter-long street, you will find food and drink stalls lining both sides of the road. On a Saigon food tour at Ho Thi Ky Food Street, you should not miss various sweet soups, snails, grilled meat skewers, hủ tiếu, crab soup, bánh cuốn, and more. The area also features unusual and unique dishes such as snail hủ tiếu, snail phá lấu, tamarind seed sweet soup, and pumpkin sweet soup.
2.4. Vinh Khanh Food Street

Another exciting destination for a Saigon food tour, especially for seafood and snail lovers, is Vinh Khanh Food Street. This street is home to numerous famous snail restaurants in Saigon, including Oc Vu, Oc Dao, Oc Oanh, Oc Thao, and more. Restaurants line both sides of the street and serve a wide variety of familiar snail and shellfish dishes, such as mud creeper snails, spider conch, sweet snails, apple snails, blood cockles, fatty snails, oysters, and crab claws. Besides snails and shellfish, you can also enjoy specialties such as snakehead fish thick noodle soup, Chau Doc fish noodle soup, and Soc Trang fermented fish noodle soup.
2.5. Nguyen Thuong Hien Food Street

Nguyen Thuong Hien Food Street brings together countless Saigon specialties, including bánh tráng trộn, chili-salted bánh mì, phá lấu, Vietnamese-style fried rice cakes, broken rice, grilled skewers, and more. In addition to enjoying a Saigon food tour, visitors to Nguyen Thuong Hien Street can also explore and shop for clothing, shoes, and other fashion items.
2.6. Ho Con Rua Snack Area

Ho Con Rua (Turtle Lake) is a familiar gathering and nightlife spot among young people. Your Saigon food tour will be even more enjoyable with the delicious street food available here, such as fish balls, beef balls, shaken mango, various types of rice paper snacks, egg cakes, Vietnamese pork and fermented pork salad, sweet bánh đúc, calamansi tea, and more. Come here in the late afternoon or evening to enjoy the food and take in the lively atmosphere!
2.7. Phan Xich Long Food Street

Phan Xich Long Food Street is home to a wide variety of establishments, from stylish cafés and restaurants to affordable eateries serving a diverse selection of Saigon street food. You can start your Saigon food tour here with dishes such as grilled fermented pork sausage, chicken rice, grilled meat with bamboo-tube sticky rice, bún chả, chili-grilled chicken, Singapore frog porridge, and more. Afterwards, stop by one of the many cafés or milk tea shops with beautiful views to enjoy a drink while watching the lively streets.
2.8. Alley 284 Le Van Sy

Alley 284 Le Van Sy is home to many delicious eateries and attracts large numbers of both locals and visitors. Your Saigon food tour will certainly be more exciting with dishes such as fermented fish noodle soup, crab thick noodle soup, bánh xèo, bún bò Huế, bún riêu, various sweet soups, yogurt, and more in this small alley. The eateries here offer a wide variety of dishes with distinctive flavors, making the area especially suitable for those who love Central Vietnamese cuisine.
2.9. Tan Dinh Night Market

Tan Dinh Market is located on Hai Ba Trung Street and mainly sells everyday necessities such as food, groceries, clothing, fabrics, flowers, and more. From afternoon until evening, food and drink stalls begin to open, making this Saigon night market especially lively. Both domestic and international visitors often come here to enjoy frog porridge, pork rib cartilage porridge, broken rice, chicken rice, and various affordable drinks. The food and beverages at the market are reasonably priced and of good quality, earning positive feedback from many diners.
3. Suggested Itinerary for a Complete Saigon Food Tour
If you are planning a Saigon food tour but are not sure what to eat or where to find delicious food, you can consider the following itinerary:
Morning: For breakfast in Saigon, you can try some of these delicious options:

items: Hoa Ma Bánh Mì: 53 Cao Thang, Ho Chi Minh City
Saigon Broken Rice: 389 Hung Phu, Ho Chi Minh City
Tan Binh Lotus Leaf Sticky Rice: 35 Ngo Thi Thu Minh, Ho Chi Minh City
Enjoy traditional Vietnamese filter coffee on Phan Dinh Phung Street

content.text: Afternoon: For lunch in Saigon, visitors can enjoy some of the city's famous dishes:

items: Thien Huong Hot Bánh Cuốn: 179A Street 3/2, Ho Chi Minh City
Kieu Bao Grilled Pork Vermicelli: 339/12 To Hien Thanh Street, Ho Chi Minh City
Vietnamese Phở: 66 Tran Quoc Toan, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: Late Afternoon: When hunger strikes in the late afternoon, you can try some delicious Saigon snacks such as:

items: Chu Vien Bánh Tráng Trộn: 38 Nguyen Thuong Hien, Ho Chi Minh City
Ha Ky Sweet Soup: 138 Chau Van Liem, Ho Chi Minh City
Trang Crab Soup: 201 Van Kiep, Ho Chi Minh City

content.text: Evening: To wrap up your Saigon food tour, enjoy dinner with some of these delicious dishes:

items: Di Nui Phá Lấu: 243/30 Ton Dan, Ho Chi Minh City
Di 9 My Tho Hủ Tiếu: 538/51 Doan Van Bo, Ho Chi Minh City
Delicious snail restaurants along Vinh Khanh Food Street, Ho Chi Minh City

title: 10 Delicious Dishes You Must Try at Least Once When Visiting Hue
excerpt: Hue cuisine is not only delicious but also incredibly affordable and beautifully presented. If you ever have the chance to visit Hue, don't miss the opportunity to enjoy its delicious, nutritious, and affordable local cuisine.
author: Thành phố Huế

content.text: Influenced by royal cuisine, Hue dishes tend to be quite elaborate. The attention to detail is evident not only in the selection and preparation of ingredients but also in the way each dish is arranged and decorated, making every serving look like a work of art.

The presentation of food here emphasizes the overall dining experience rather than simply eating until full. Diners can enjoy the food not only through their sense of taste but also through sight, sound, and smell.

Hue preserves more than 1,000 distinctive dishes from the ancient capital, including royal dishes once served to the emperors of the Nguyen Dynasty, ranging from everyday rustic food to luxurious delicacies. Among them are 10 signature dishes that no visitor to Hue should miss.
Bún Bò Huế (Hue Beef Noodle Soup)
The first dish you should try when visiting Hue is bún bò Huế. This dish carries the distinctive flavors of Hue, so the name of the city has become an inseparable part of the dish's name.

The main ingredients include beef shank, pork knuckles, and pork blood pudding. Some versions also contain rare beef and crab sausage. The dish is usually served with fresh herbs, banana blossom, and bean sprouts.

The broth of Hue bún bò is usually seasoned with a small amount of shrimp paste to create its distinctive flavor. It has a characteristic reddish color, a naturally sweet taste, and a rich flavor that remains satisfying to the very last drop.
Recommended places:

O Cuong Chu Diep Hue Beef Noodle Soup. Address: 6 Tran Truc Nhan, Hue City. Opening hours: 6:30 AM - 10:00 AM. Price: VND 15,000 - 30,000. Other options include O Phuong Hue Beef Noodle Soup - 24 Nguyen Khuyen; Ba Tuyet Hue Beef Noodle Soup - 47 Nguyen Cong Tru.
Bánh Bột Lọc (Tapioca Dumplings)

These dumplings are made from refined tapioca starch and filled with shrimp seasoned with various spices. The filling can also be made with pork or a combination of shrimp and pork. The dumplings are wrapped in banana leaves.
The dumplings are cooked by steaming or boiling. They are served with dipping sauce to enhance their rich flavor.
Bánh bột lọc has a pleasantly chewy texture from the tapioca wrapper and a rich, fragrant filling of shrimp and pork.
Recommended place: Chi Banh Restaurant on Nguyen Trai Street.
Bánh Bèo (Steamed Rice Cakes)
Bánh bèo is usually served in small bowls, about the size of a dipping-sauce bowl. The main ingredient is rice flour, topped with scallion oil and crispy pork cracklings.

The highlight of this dish is the dipping sauce. On its own, the dish mainly has the rich flavor of the pork cracklings and the fragrance of scallions, and can taste rather bland. However, when combined with a dipping sauce made from shrimp cooking broth, fish sauce, and a few slices of chili, the flavor of the dish comes alive.
Bánh Nậm (Flat Rice Dumplings)

Bánh nậm is another traditional specialty of Hue, similar to bánh bột lọc and bánh bèo. It is made from rice flour and filled with mung beans or minced shrimp and pork. The dumpling is served with diluted fish sauce and chili. It has a fragrant, rich flavor and such a delicate texture that it seems to melt in your mouth.

Because the dumplings are very delicate, diners should use a spoon rather than chopsticks. Place the dumpling on a plate, unwrap the banana leaf, drizzle dipping sauce over the top, then use a spoon to gently separate it from the leaf before eating.
Recommended place: THUY & Bánh Bèo – Nậm – Lọc. Address: 16 Pham Hong Thai. Opening hours: 12:30 PM – 8:00 PM (afternoon). Price: VND 10,000 – 20,000.
Bánh Ướt (Steamed Rice Rolls)
The wrapper is made primarily from rice flour, which is steamed into a thin layer. Varieties include bánh ướt with grilled pork, bánh ướt with fermented shrimp, and more.
The rice sheets are soft, smooth, and served hot, with fillings such as wood ear mushrooms and minced pork. They are topped with fried shallots and served with dipping sauce and fresh herbs.

Recommended places: Bánh Ướt Restaurant at 44 Tran Truc Nhan, Huyen Anh Restaurant at 55 Kim Long, or Chi Ha Restaurant at 29 Le Hong Phong. A plate of bánh ướt costs only around VND 15,000 - 20,000 per bowl.
Cơm Hến and Other Clam Dishes
For as little as VND 10,000, diners can enjoy an authentic Hue-style bowl of cơm hến. You may be surprised to receive such a generous serving of clam rice for just a small amount of money.

This dish is a mixture of white rice, stir-fried baby clams, crispy pork cracklings, fried shallots, and various fresh herbs. A little shrimp paste and fish sauce are added to enhance the aroma before everything is mixed together.
The soft rice combines with the salty and slightly spicy seasoning, crispy pork cracklings, naturally sweet clam broth, and the chewy sweetness of the clams to create the dish's unique character.
Clams served with crispy rice crackers are also a popular choice among diners.
Recommended place: The best place to enjoy cơm hến is Con Hen, Vy Da Ward.
Some specific places you can consider include:

items: Ty Hon Restaurant - No. 3 Han Mac Tu
Nho Restaurant - No. 28 Pham Hong Thai

content.text: You can also try other clam dishes at these restaurants, such as clam vermicelli, which is similar to cơm hến but uses vermicelli instead of rice; clam porridge; or clams served with crispy rice crackers.
Hue Sweet Soups (Chè Huế)
Visiting Hue without trying its sweet soups would be a major omission. One of the most famous sweet soup spots in Hue is the small alley sweet soup shop on Hung Vuong Street.
The shop is tucked away deep inside an alley, creating a quiet atmosphere. Inside, several small wooden tables are arranged closely together.
At the counter, tall glasses filled with colorful sweet soups in various flavors are neatly arranged and ready to serve. Customers only need to add ice before enjoying them.

Available varieties include corn sweet soup, purple sweet potato sweet soup, glutinous rice dumpling sweet soup, mung bean sweet soup, basil seed sweet soup, hyacinth bean sweet soup, red bean sweet soup, tapioca dumplings with roasted pork, and more.

Among them, tapioca dumplings with roasted pork are the most unusual dish and one that everyone wants to try. Transparent tapioca dumplings are filled with neatly cut pieces of roasted pork, including the crispy skin. The sweet soup combines sweet and savory flavors with a chewy, crispy, and rich texture. Purple sweet potato sweet soup, meanwhile, is a favorite among many diners thanks to its gentle purple color combined with rich, fragrant coconut milk.
Address: Chè Hẻm, No. 1, Alley 29 Hung Vuong, Hue City. Opening hours: 2:00 PM - 10:00 PM. Price: VND 5,000 - 12,000 per glass.
Vegetarian Vermicelli (Bún Chay)
Although it is a vegetarian dish, bún chay is in no way inferior to any meat-based noodle dish. This reflects the sophistication of Hue's culinary culture.
It still features an appealing golden-red color and a naturally sweet, flavorful broth, but its ingredients contain no animal fat.

The ingredients are entirely plant-based, usually consisting of vegetables, roots, fruits, and various mushrooms, skillfully combined with seasonings to create a dish that is nutritious, wholesome, and distinctive.
Mixed Balut (Trứng Vịt Lộn Trộn)
This unique dish can be found at the corner of Nguyen Trai and Yet Kieu Streets, next to a helmet shop.
The stall only operates in the evening. It is located on the sidewalk with around three plastic tables, yet it attracts many customers who eat there or order takeaway.

Customers can order plain balut, which is served whole with a side of pickled vegetables. Alternatively, they can order mixed balut, in which case the owner prepares and mixes the ingredients before serving the finished dish.

The mixed balut consists of peeled balut eggs, pickled vegetables including fig and julienned green mango, Vietnamese coriander, and various seasonings skillfully combined to create a dish that feels both familiar and unusual.
The combination of spicy, crunchy, fragrant, and subtly sweet flavors makes this dish especially appealing.
Price: only around VND 7,000 per egg.
Salt Coffee (Cà Phê Muối)
If Hanoi is famous for egg coffee, Hue has salt coffee - a signature specialty of the ancient capital.

When people hear the name salt coffee, they may imagine a coffee with the strong salty taste of seawater. However, that does not fully capture the flavor of this unique drink. Salt coffee still has the enticing aroma of coffee, the rich creaminess of fresh milk, a gentle salty note, and a mild bitterness that lingers at the end.

Customers can choose to drink it hot or add ice. This is perhaps one of the unique features of salt coffee: it can be enjoyed either hot or cold while retaining its original flavor without becoming diluted.
Recommended places: 142 Dang Thai Luan; 10 Nguyen Luong Bang. Price: VND 15,000 - 20,000 per glass.

There are also several other famous Hue dishes you can try if you have the opportunity, such as Nam Pho thick noodle soup at 347 Chi Lang; bánh khoái at 11 Pho Duc Chinh; and Ba Doi thick noodle soup at 75 Nguyen Trai.
